newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH ELECTION VIEW UPDATE -POLITICIANS' COMMENTS.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH ELECTION VIEW UPDATE -POLITICIANS' COMMENTS.

text.p: Following are comments from politicians after the left was projected to win a runoff vote in France's parliamentary election over the ruling centre-right RPR/UDF coalition.
LIONEL JOSPIN, SOCIALIST PARTY LEADER
The overwhelming feeling that this very important election inspires for me is one of a deep demand from our people.
It's a reasoned and pressing demand for real long-term progress for the French people, especially the least favoured.

(It is) a demand for justice, a demand for a profound renewal of our public life and democracy, a demand for an economic and social policy put at the service of man, a demand for a reorientation of European construction -- which we favour -- and a demand for a scupulous attention to the problems French people meet in their daily lives.
ALAIN JUPPE, FORMER PRIME MINISTER

We did not manage to convince the French people that we were going in the right direction. The people have spoken. Their decision is sovereign. We all respect it. I wish good luck to those who will now govern France and I wish good luck to France.
LAURENT FABIUS, FORMER SOCIALIST PRIME MINISTER

Things must be done gradually. It's true that we have to make significant moves as people have voted for a certain relaunch of consumption which in itself will lead to a ceratin development of growth.
At the same time, it would not make sense to take measures which would end up hurting those who should be beneficiaries.

We have to respect the course that has been set - we have signed a common declaration (Socialist and Communist parties) and at the same time do things which are positive for everyone and above all not to penalise companies because we need companies which work.
PIERRE MAUROY, FORMER SOCIALIST PRIME MINISTER
How could you imagine another prime minister (than Lionel Jospin)? He was a great artisan of this victory for the left. He had the merit to explain the left's programme, to do it in a pedagogic way.

The government should include everything that the left now represents. There has to be the left, of course, the Communists, the Greens, doubtlessly a representative of the Radical party and the Citizens' Movement.
NICOLAS SARKOZY, FORMER BUDGET MINISTER (RPR)

This is defeat, it is indisputable. We are in a democracy, we must accept it...I am sad and a bit angry because I am convinced that our ideas were not defeated, but the way in which they were defended was.
BERNARD PONS, OUTGOING TRANSPORT MINISTER

This is a failure for the majority. The Socialists will now have the responsibility to govern. They have made a lot of promises, I'd like to point to two of them -- 700,000 jobs for young people and 35 hours paid as 39. We will closely monitor how they follow up.
The government worked well but was badly understood by the French people and disliked.
JEAN-MARIE LE PEN, NATIONAL FRONT

This is not a defeat, it is a disaster. Jacques Chirac has been beaten twice, in votes on the first round and in seats on the second. He played double or quits and lost. He should draw the consequences and hand his mandate back to the people.
ROBERT HUE, COMMUNIST PARTY LEADER

The left must respond to the expectations of our people and choose a radically new policy...This is possible on the bases set out in our joint declaration of April 29 (with the Socialist Party) outlining our policy guidelines.
The Communist Party's approach aims at participating in the government of France. We face these questions and we will assume our responsibilities.
I have made proposals to (Socialist leader) Lionel Jospin, I want these to be discussed and I believe we can move forward.
FRANCOIS LEOTARD, HEAD OF UDF
Let us enter a new period of opposition that we will try to make as short as possible.
EDOUARD BALLADUR, FORMER PRIME MINISTER (RPR)
The result is due to the disappointment of a large part of voters, who believe the policies for which they voted has been been put into action enough.
DOMINIQUE VOYNET, GREENS LEADER
The pink-red-green alliance worked very well because our voters wanted guarantees that we would take in ecology as we enter the 21st century.
Our national council will meet tomorrow. I will plead for going to the end of our aproach so that we join the cabinet.
MARTINE AUBRY, SOCIALIST FORMER LABOUR MINISTER
I think that what the French people expressed today was that they wanted change. They expressed confidence in the Socialist programme.
MICHEL ROCARD, FORMER SOCIALIST PRIME MINISTER

The suddenness and unexpected nature of this result will create lots of anxiety and lots of hard feelings within the country. I would like to say to all of those who are feeling this loss that we are all French citizens, that we intend to govern France in the broadest possible sense of its interests, that the vision of our politics must be more open and more tolerant than it has been, and that we have no intention of affronting anyone.
-- Paris Newsroom +33 1 42 21 53 81
